Dota 2 deserves its intimidating reputation, and it probably won’t suit you if you’re looking to play casually. There’s a huge time investment before you can even enjoy a game, let alone feel competent at it. But once you start to learn its secrets, there’s a wild and exciting variety of play here that’s unmatched, even by its peers. It’s a challenge of knowledge as well as reflexes, and success is a rush. The fact that it’s completely and totally free to play in the way we wish all free-to-play games could be isn’t just one of the most generous propositions anywhere in gaming, it creates a level playing field where skill and cooperation is paramount. May the best team win.

Dota 2 is a game that requires practice, patience and a positive attitude to succeed. While the basic fundamental principles of the game remain unchanged from its earliest incarnation, the meta and dynamic is constantly and ever-changing. Of all the major RTS/MOBA games on the market, Dota 2 provides the most challenging, in depth and unique experience.

If you dream of "going pro" then Dota 2 is a game where anyone can become an e-sports legend if they've got the skill to back it up. Major tournaments including the annual International tournament have open qualifiers with no rank/MMR requirement. All you have to do is beat the competition.

Dota 2 matches can get spicy. Don't get caught up in the negativity, mom-bashing and cancer-wishing. While you're angrily banging away at your keyboard, the other team is winning. Also, Dota 2 isn't a game that holds your hand. I recommend reading Purge's Welcome to Dota, you suck[purgegamers.true.io] for all new players. You can also check out this Dota 2 Quickstart Guide on Steam.

Warning: If your free time consists of constantly raging that everyone else is ruining your life because you lost a game or claiming that you're being persecuted just because you called a *few* people a "♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥ing ♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" then you should uninstall immediately.

If you push through this, which isn't so bad if you have some friends to show you the ropes and get you into it, you will have access to a high action strategy game with so many variables to each game that you can always be suprised no matter how long you've played.

Dota 2 is more than just a game—it's a battlefield where every match feels like an epic showdown. The learning curve is steep, but once you get the hang of it, there's no turning back. The combination of intense team play, deep strategy, and high skill ceiling makes every victory feel incredibly rewarding. The hero diversity ensures that no two games are ever the same, keeping you hooked for hours. Whether you're here for the thrill of competition or the satisfaction of outplaying your opponents, Dota 2 delivers every time. Dive in and prepare for the ride of your life!

As a newish player (ignore the hours, I played this game allll the way back in like 2012 and haven't touched it till now), jumped in for the big update, and I find the new map to be fun. Having a blast playing support/offlane, and learning the game. I used to play League, but have quit a few years back due to me disliking the direction they took the game- this game gives me back that old, addicting feel of just having to play one more game.

On a more serious note, I think the game is more fair than League. In League, I often found myself thinking, "There was nothing I could have done there to save myself or turn this teamfight around." This game gives you options; items don't matter as much as they do in League, rather, it's pure level scaling, matchups, clever map positioning, using line of sight, and when it comes down to it, skill.

That being said, it still has the old MOBA problem of, even if you win your lane, another lane on your team can feed so hard that the game is unwinnable, and there's nothing much you can do about it but turtle and pray for a comeback. Stomps are prevalent, but I have noticed this game has more of a chance to turn around games than League does.

If you like MOBA's, or RTS's, or both, give this a try. It's a good blend of both!

Dota 2

Dota 2 is good game. It has a very steep learning curve. However, when you finally learn how the complex mechanics work. It can be quite fun when you pull off great ability combos. I would recommend getting a squad of at least three friends to play, preferrably experienced players who are not quick to get angry. This will make your team more organised and efficient. Communication is really important.

Secondly, it will be a safer learning environment for new players. If you ever enter a solo match, changes of getting a toxic team member is fairly high. However, there are also many patient veterans who will give constructive feedback. Pic your teammates wisely if you can.

Dota 2 is a well made game and balanced. OP characters always get nerfed eventually except for Phantom Assassin. As said before, it can be very fun when you get really cool people in a match. It can also be frustrating if you get people who do not speak your language or people who just are toxic. If you constantly get the latter, you may want to take a break from the game for a while. Just like many others have said, this game can be really addictive.

Grade 8/10

Getting into Dota 2 split my gaming life into a very distinct Before and After. Every game I'd played before Dota now felt boring and repetitive to go back to. Every game that I'll ever play after has to deal with me comparing it to Dota (Dota wins every time). That's probably the greatest compliment I could ever give to a video game, and I'm glad this is the multiplayer game I chose to spend time on all those years ago.

EDIT for the Steam badge: I still feel the same way about Dota as I did 8 years ago when I wrote that first review, and I think that speaks for itself.

I’ve been playing since Warcraft III back in 2006, and I moved to Dota 2 in 2014. I stopped in 2024 and only came back last month but coming back made me realize something I’ve never really said out loud.

When everything in my life starts falling apart, Dota is the one thing that’s always there.

It sounds dramatic for a game, but it’s the truth. There were moments where I didn’t know what to do, where things felt heavy, confusing, or just empty and somehow, queuing up for a match gave me something to hold onto. A reason to stay focused. A way to get through another day.

It’s not perfect. It can be frustrating, toxic, exhausting. But even then, it never left. It gave me structure when I had none, something familiar when everything else felt uncertain.

I’m still here, typing this, because I had something to come back to.

So yeah this isn’t just a game to me. It’s been a constant in a life that hasn’t always been stable.

Thank you for that.
